newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso ends soft on year-end dollar cover.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso ends soft on year-end dollar cover.

text.p: The Mexican peso closed slightly weaker on Monday due to demand to close year-end dollar positions in what traders said was a quiet session ahead of the New Year holiday on Wednesday.
"Dealers buying dollars early on to cover positions weakened the peso a little, but the market in general was very quiet," a trader said.
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour stablemate closed 0.9 and 0.4 of a centavo weaker, respectively, at 7.8520/7.8570 and 7.8440/7.8480 per dollar.
Same-day peso contracts closed earlier 0.85 of a centavo weaker at 7.8400/7.8450 per dollar.
Dealers said demand also arose for 48-hour contracts as they did not need to be paid for until Thursday and with pesos that could, meanwhile, be invested in the local money market.
Traders did not expect forecast falls in Cetes rates at the primary auction, to be held later in the day, to weaken the peso on Tuesday.
"The idea is that the auction results should not hurt the peso, so we do not expect any sharp changes," a trader said.
Money market traders said they expected primary rates on bellwether 28-day Cetes to fall by up to 75 basis points.
